interface.name: TemperatureSensorInput
interface.description: The input value of the temperature sensor, i.e., the actual temperature

interface.name: OverheatProtection
interface.description: Display of the overheating protection status

interface.name: HeaterOutput
interface.description: The control output of the heater

scan_semantics: At scan k, inputs I[k] are sampled once, q[k] is pre-scan retained state, outputs O[k] are observed after execution, and q[k+1] is the updated state. Each test creates a fresh FB instance before step 0. An initialized instance has not yet executed a scan. Timer elapsed time is zero on the first eligible sampled invocation; dt_ms is elapsed wall time since the previous invocation, not automatically a synthetic input to the FB. No unobserved past input stability is assumed. All sequences here are expected values.
safety_priority: Sensor fault or active overheat protection overrides the heat demand.
Protection shutdown is evaluated before the output is finalized.
assumptions: At equality TemperatureSensorInput=SetTemperature, retain the last heat-demand state. On a fresh instance the retained demand is FALSE.

The prose says "more than" a period and gives 5s. The evaluation resolves this to a 5-second threshold: protection trips at continuous heating elapsed>=5s, beginning with elapsed zero at the first energized sample.
Protection is latched for at least 3s from its trip. At elapsed>=3s it may clear and heat can restart in the same scan if the sensor is valid and demand remains.
A sensor fault immediately turns heat off and resets continuous-heating time. It does not clear or restart an already active cooldown.
The display outputs mirror their corresponding sampled temperature and setpoint even during a fault. HeaterStatus equals HeaterOutput. Inputs are held stable between timed samples.

formal_properties.explanation: Invalid sensor data must never energize the heater.
The heater remains off during cooldown.
The status output reports actual commanded heat.
A permitted heat demand energizes the heater.
The continuous-heating threshold trips protection in the same scan.
Protection cannot clear before its cooldown expires.
With advancing time and persistent valid demand, heating resumes after finite cooldown.

atomic_propositions.demand: Ghost retained demand; set below setpoint, clear above, retain at equality.
atomic_propositions.heatLimitReached: Continuous energized time has reached 5s, with first energized scan at elapsed zero.
atomic_propositions.cooldownDone: At least 3s has elapsed since protection trip.
atomic_propositions.interface names: Identically named sampled input or observed output.
